newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ex-Dutch air cargo to Americas busy, Africa quieter.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Dutch air cargo to Americas busy, Africa quieter.

text.p: Air cargo markets to North and Latin America ex-Amsterdam are relatively active at the moment, despite the fact that February is usually a slow month, a Reuters survey shows.
The ex-Amsterdam market to Africa was stable but less active.

The North American market was described as stable, by an American Airlines respresentative in the Netherlands. But competition is still fierce, with many freighters operating between the Netherlands and the U.S., he added.
Electronics products and vegetables such as tomatoes and cucumbers are major exports to the U.S.

Rates to the U.S. are increasing in all the major markets. This has been much-needed, he said, after very low rates on some routes last year. American Airlines will probably increase its rates by between five and ten percent in the beginning of April, he said.
Fred Veenendaal, director of Air Canada's general sales agent VIA, said the North American market is relatively good for the time of year. Air Canada is actually above target this year, he added.
The strength of the dollar means the North Americans are buying more from Europe, he said. Rates too are stable and have not seen their usual dip in February.
He is also optimistic concerning prospects in March. Textiles, electronics and livestock are major exports to Canada, he added.

Managing director of Zygene, Jos van der Woensel, general sales agent for Delta Air Lines, said the North American market has been surprisingly strong in January and February, compared to this time last year and Latin America too, is also very strong.

"If it continues like this we may even need a freighter to North America!" he said. The strong dollar is a factor in the growth in the market, he added, and this seems to be assuring a steady and stable pace of growth.
Delta Airline's Netherlands capacity will double effectively from June 2, said van der Woensel.

The Netherlands has been sharing the Delta aircraft with Stuttgart and Prague but from June the service will fly directly between the Netherlands and the U.S. which means 24 tonnes of space will be available (12 tonnes to New York and 12 to Atlanta), he added.
Zygene also represents LanChile and demand is extremely strong to Chile and Argentina especially, he said.
A spokesman for Air Cargo Trader which is a GSA for Fast Air, Aeroperu and Canadian Airlines amongst others said Latin America has certainly improved compared to last year.
Mexico was a particular hot spot, with trade from the Netherlands expanding rapidly, he added.

Canadian Airlines is an off-line carrier out of the Netherlands therefore the company trucks any cargo to London. Mainly this is vegetables destined for the North American market but currently it is not the Dutch growing season.

The buoyancy of the Latin American market has proved so strong that Dutch carrier Martinair will be starting two new services to serve the Latin America in March, said the carrier's cargo sales manager, Gerard ter Bruggen.

On March 5, the carrier will be doubling the frequency of its weekly Chile service to Santiago. The MD-11 freighter service will then depart ex-Netherlands on Mondays and Wednesdays. Business to the region has picked up rapidly, he said. Exports from the Netherlands include telecommunications equipment, car parts, chemicals, spares and foodstuffs.
Bogota is also a market where there is very strong demand, he added. The Dutch airline has a weekly MD-11 freighter service to Bogota.

As well as the extra Santiago service, Martinair will be putting a freighter into Miami to serve the Latin American market on March 5. There are many projects going on in the region, especially telecommunications projects, said ter Bruggen. This Miami freighter service will be retained through the summer season, in addition to the carrier's five-time-weekly passenger services to Miami.
Martinair is unusual in that the carrier converts its aircraft into freighters or passenger aircraft depending on the season and demand.
This summer season it will retain four full freighter configurated aircraft throughout the year, he added. Last year, the carrier only kept three in freighter configuration.

On April 1, Martinair will be increasing its rates from between five to ten percent. Cargo rates to the U.S. and South Africa will increase by five percent, whereas rates to the Latin American region will rise by five to ten percent.
All industry sources contacted said the latest round of rate rises announced by the carriers will be accepted as fair increases by the air cargo industry.

Southern Africa it seems, is a strange market at the moment. Frits de Bois, cargo manager of South African Airways said the market has started to increase again after the South African holidays in December and January.

However, there does seem to be a trend he said for shippers to send their cargo at the weekends which means the mid-week flights are not so busy. "There is enough for everyone to have a slice of the cake at the weekend but mid-week it is quiet," he said.
Martinair started flights to South Africa late last year and it too also offers mid-week flights.
Rates to South Africa, though despite the extra competition from Martinair have been relatively stable, he added.
On March 1, the South African carrier will increase its rates by five to ten percent. Cargo rates to South Africa are hovering between 4.0 and 4.50 guilders.

A source from Air Namibia said currently the market is quiet but it is expected to pick-up in March. Netherlands cargo is sent via Frankfurt or London normally to Namibia. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
